summary.title: Particles
summary.one_liner: You learn how to build a simple 2D particle system in OpenGL, with particle structs, respawning dead particles, additive blending, and a particle generator that trails the ball in Breakout.
keywords: how to make particle trail in opengl
takeaways: Store particles in a fixed-size pool with a life value, and respawn the first dead particle instead of growing the list.
Use a search that starts from the last used index to find a dead particle quickly, with a linear fallback.
Update each particle by decreasing its life by delta time, moving it, and fading its alpha while it is alive.
Render particles as textured quads with an offset and color uniform, using additive blending (GL_SRC_ALPHA, GL_ONE) for a glowing look.
Wrap the logic in a ParticleGenerator class and draw particles before the ball so they appear behind it in Breakout.
summary.summary: The tutorial explains how particle systems work and builds one for the Breakout game from the LearnOpenGL 2D game series. It shows a Particle struct with position, velocity, color and life, then walks through spawning new particles each frame, reusing dead particles via a first-unused search, and updating and fading them. Rendering uses a simple vertex and fragment shader pair with per-particle offset and color uniforms, drawn with additive blending. The page ends by wrapping this in a ParticleGenerator class that follows the ball.
